title: A short history of the bicycle
text:
The first machine that looked like a bicycle was built in 1817 {A}. It had no pedals, so riders pushed themselves along with their feet. Half a century later, French engineers {B} pedals to the front wheel, {C} the ride was also much more dangerous. The 'penny-farthing', with its enormous front wheel, was fashionable among young men {D}.

The decisive change came in the 1880s with the 'safety bicycle'. Both wheels were of equal size and a chain drove the rear one, {E}. Suddenly, cycling was open to everybody. Women in particular welcomed the new freedom, {F}.

Today more than a billion bicycles are in use around the world. In crowded cities they are often quicker than cars, they cost little to maintain and they produce no fumes. Many municipalities now build special lanes to protect cyclists, and some employers even pay people who cycle to work. Cities from Copenhagen to Bogotá regularly close whole streets to cars on Sundays so that families can ride in safety.
